case_analysis.focal_point: Whether a congressionally approved interstate compact, specifically the Waterfront Commission Compact, requires mutual assent for a signatory state to withdraw, in the absence of an express provision to the contrary.
case_analysis.legal_provision: The Waterfront Commission Compact (an interstate compact approved by Congress).
case_analysis.petitioner_position: New York argues that the Waterfront Commission Compact bars New Jersey from withdrawing without New York's consent. New York asserts that, in the absence of an express provision allowing unilateral withdrawal, the compact requires mutual assent for either state to withdraw. They contend that permitting unilateral withdrawal would undermine the fundamental purpose of interstate compacts to forge stable and lasting solutions.
case_analysis.respondent_position: New Jersey argues that the Waterfront Commission Compact does not preclude unilateral withdrawal. New Jersey contends that because the Compact does not expressly 'cabin' or forbid withdrawal, it is permitted. They suggest that the 'far better inference' is that the parties drafted the Compact without intending to preclude unilateral withdrawal, implying a default rule that allows unilateral withdrawal unless expressly forbidden. New Jersey also argues that states may prefer the ability to opt out of a compact when circumstances change.
